target_customer: Large enterprises whose HR, IT and finance teams answer employee questions and tickets
problem: HR and IT teams spend much of their time answering repetitive employee questions and tickets, while employees wait for simple answers. Leena AI built a virtual assistant that answers inside Slack or Teams.
business_model: Enterprise B2B SaaS sold through direct sales, priced by employees or modules
product_category: Enterprise conversational AI for HR, IT and finance helpdesks

founders.name: Adit Jain
education: IIT Delhi (company blog says the three founders met there)
previous_startups: Chatteron, the earlier chatbot-building product, later became Leena AI (TechCrunch 2018)
founders.background_notes: The company name story says the founders were runners-up in a global computer vision competition as undergraduates.

founders.name: Mayank Goyal
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and named as a co-founder (first name only) on the company blog.

founders.name: Anand Kumar Prajapati
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and named as a co-founder (first name only) on the company blog.

competitors.name: Espressive
competitors.what: AI virtual support agent (Barista) for employee IT and HR questions

competitors.name: Talla
competitors.what: AI chatbot service desk for IT and HR questions
competitors.funding_then: 8.3M Series A led by Glasswing Ventures, June 2017

technical_complexity.rationale: Natural language understanding in 2018 needed custom intent models plus integrations with HR systems such as Oracle, SAP and NetSuite and with chat channels.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations into enterprise HR systems and customer knowledge bases create lock-in, but rivals such as Espressive and Talla offered the same wedge and large language models later lowered the model barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large vendors and Moveworks, Glean and Copilot Studio later built overlapping assistants. In October 2025 Axios reported Leena AI approached ServiceNow about buying part of Moveworks; no deal was confirmed.

market_need_then: Enterprises with thousands of employees had large HR shared service desks. In September 2018 Leena AI reported 16 enterprise customers and a goal of 50 in 12 to 18 months (TechCrunch).

branding.name_origin: Derived from Lena Forsen, the Swedish model whose photograph became a standard test image for face recognition; the founders, runners-up in a computer vision contest, used it as a light hearted nod (company blog). Earlier company name was Chatteron per TechCrunch.
branding.domain_note: leena.ai in use; acquisition detail not found

identity.mascot_or_character: Named AI Colleagues: Harrison for HR, Iris for IT, Fiona for Finance (company site)
identity.visual_style: Enterprise SaaS style per company site
identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise and ROI focused with some humor in the founder blog post

branding.brand_signature: Human named AI Colleagues for each back-office function

rebrands.why: Shift from a chatbot-building tool to an HR assistant product (TechCrunch 2018)

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found of fan or merch communities; brand awareness comes from enterprise sales and analyst recognition such as Gartner.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct human name used consistently, but evidence of broad recognition is limited to enterprise buyers and analyst mentions.

pivots.from: Chatteron, a tool to help others build chatbots
pivots.to: HR assistant for enterprise employees (Leena AI)
pivots.why: Per TechCrunch the company shifted its focus to HR; the exact date is not stated precisely and sources differ on the year

pivots.to: Agentic AI platform with AI Colleagues for the back office
pivots.why: Company positioning on its site and Bessemer Atlas profile; exact date not sourced

outcome_analysis: Leena AI graduated from YC with a 2M seed, sold to large enterprises on a repeatable sales motion, and raised an 8M Series A in 2020 and a 30M Series B in 2021, with total funding about 40M. The company still operates, now repositioned as an agentic back-office platform, and faces large rivals such as Moveworks, Glean and Microsoft. Its headcount and sales outcomes since 2021 are only partly reported.
notes: Series A source is the company blog title and search summary (8M, Greycroft lead) and was not opened; two outlets (Inc42, TechCrunch) agree on 8M. The founded year is 2015 per TechCrunch while VentureBeat says 2018 and Wikipedia says Chatteron preceded Leena AI. Round list and the company's statement of over 40M raised agree with the three rounds. Moveworks 2018 funding not found. Elad Gil is a 2018 seed investor, not in the 2021 round.
